functions/customer-text-cleanup.md.text:
Customer Text Cleanup

Frozen 4.0 — real-world import text contracts

## 1. Name and Classification **Customer text cleanup — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:trim-space](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-trim-space), [fn:pad-string](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-pad-string), [fn:characters](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-characters), [fn:graphemes](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-graphemes) and [fn:char](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-char). Initial char/characters delivery: [PR #82](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/82), [40ebaa79](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/40ebaa79032b17fc45d6d3bb3e58cb00e2fda742), REQ-118 S0/S1 part 1. Remaining string functions: [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39), S1 part 2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-12** against immutable [QT4CG source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). The eight reviewed function definitions are unchanged from the earlier a014e1b4 review pin. This does not recover unavailable historical adopted specification snapshots. ## 2. Intent Trim import padding from a customer label while preserving its interior spacing and Unicode spelling. Report codepoint and grapheme counts separately, and pad an export value to a minimum codepoint length. ## 3. Also Known As Boundary trimming, minimum-length padding and character segmentation are descriptive terms. No function aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can trim XML whitespace with two anchored regular-expression replacements, split codepoints with string-to-codepoints/codepoints-to-string, and append repeated padding explicitly. The complete comparison returns the same cleaned and padded label. It omits the grapheme count: XPath 3.1 has no direct standard grapheme-segmentation function. `normalize-space` would also collapse interior runs and therefore implements a different cleanup rule. ## 5. Motivation A customer name can contain deliberately repeated interior spaces, a combining accent and a supplementary character. Treating UTF-16 storage units, Unicode codepoints and displayed clusters as interchangeable gives misleading length checks. The report makes the import/export contract explicit. ## 6. Language Alignment `trim-space` removes XML whitespace (space, tab, CR and LF) at the selected start/end/both boundary. It preserves interior whitespace and does not remove NBSP. Empty input returns an empty string. `pad-string` defaults to end padding with spaces; options select side and padding. It never truncates. Both-side odd padding puts the extra character at the end. `characters` returns one string per Unicode codepoint; `graphemes` groups supported combining/ZWJ sequences into clusters. Neither performs Unicode normalization. `char` constructs a string from a positive codepoint, recognized entity name or supported escape; some entity names return multiple codepoints. It is not an HTML document decoder. Bosak's [Graphemes_1/GraphemeClusterClass implementation](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs) approximates segmentation: it does not distinguish Hangul jamo, Prepend, regional-indicator or full Indic/extended-pictographic classes. These verified combining-mark and ZWJ cases do not establish complete Unicode grapheme conformance. ## 7. Applicability Use for import boundary cleanup and codepoint-length export rules. The fixture's target length is a minimum of ten codepoints, not bytes, screen columns or grapheme clusters. Padding does not make emoji and Latin characters equally wide in a font. A Unicode normalization policy or complete grapheme implementation is a separate requirement. The examples do not truncate customer names or claim to validate them. ## 8. Structure Read a name element, trim its boundaries, count codepoints and supported grapheme clusters, then append dots to reach ten codepoints. Construct an em-dash separator with char(8212). ## 9. Participants The customer element supplies unnormalized text. Cleanup preserves interior content. Segmentation describes length under two models. Padding produces the export field. A report shows all outputs. ## 10. Collaborations Trim before padding. Keep the original combining sequence when preservation is required. Use count(characters(...)) for the specified codepoint contract; do not substitute grapheme count for that minimum-length rule. ## 11. Consequences The fixture retains two interior spaces and a decomposed accent. Its eight codepoints form seven supported grapheme clusters; two dots reach ten codepoints. Oversized values remain unchanged. Invalid side/padding options and unsupported char values raise the demonstrated errors. Known grapheme limitations remain documented rather than being certified by these samples. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles XML boundary whitespace, interior preservation, nontruncating codepoint padding; Character/entity conversion and supported grapheme clusters; Defaults, empty values, side options and invalid input. **Boundaries:** Grapheme segmentation is approximate; missing keywords, implicit trim focus and unknown-option validation are not supported contracts. Follow-up groups: F01, F02, F03, F13. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new calls with CompileOptions.Compatibility40; the default 3.1 profile rejects them. The comparison uses Compatibility31. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact text/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. Unicode inputs are inline XML character references so their intended values are explicit. **Supplementary text-contract review (2026-10-12):** [Eight-family contract review](../TEXT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed label/filename README](../examples/text-contracts/README.md) supply explicit keyword refusals at 3.1/4.0/experimental, positional defaults/empty/invalid cases and complete paired reports. Numeric substring/option tolerance and validation boundaries remain observed follow-ups; the review does not implement keywords or certify full Unicode/coercion conformance. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input; the name contains e followed by combining acute, two interior spaces and a truck emoji: ```xml José 🚚 ``` ### Complete XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/main.xpath): ```xpath let $name := string(parse-xml(' José 🚚 ')/customer/name) let $label := trim-space($name) return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(characters($label)), '; graphemes=', count(graphemes($label)), '; export=[', pad-string($label, 10, map {'padding': '.'}), ']; separator=', char(8212)) ``` Exact output: ```text label=[José 🚚]; codepoints=8; graphemes=7; export=[José 🚚..]; separator=— ``` ### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison [Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $name := string(parse-xml(' José 🚚 ')/customer/name) return let $label := replace(replace($name, '^\s+', ''), '\s+$', '') return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(string-to-codepoints($label)), '; export=[', $label, string-join(for $i in 1 to max((0, 10 - string-length($label))) return '.', ''), ']; separator=', codepoints-to-string(8212)) ``` Exact output: ```text label=[José 🚚]; codepoints=8; export=[José 🚚..]; separator=— ``` ### Boundary and error inventory Each file embeds its complete input. Brackets make significant spaces visible. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/main.xpath) | `label=[José 🚚]; codepoints=8; graphemes=7; export=[José 🚚..]; separator=—` | | [baseline](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/baseline.xpath) | `label=[José 🚚]; codepoints=8; export=[José 🚚..]; separator=—` | | [preserve-interior](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/preserve-interior.xpath) | `[Ada Lovelace]` | | [nbsp-preserved](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/nbsp-preserved.xpath) | `160` | | [trim-start](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/trim-start.xpath) | `[Ada ]` | | [empty-trim](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/empty-trim.xpath) | `0` | | [pad-both](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/pad-both.xpath) | `**Ada***` | | [never-truncate](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/never-truncate.xpath) | `Lovelace` | | [empty-pad](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/empty-pad.xpath) | `...` | | [codepoint-split](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/codepoint-split.xpath) | `101,769` | | [combining-grapheme](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/combining-grapheme.xpath) | `1` | | [emoji-zwj](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/emoji-zwj.xpath) | `1` | | [empty-characters](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/empty-characters.xpath) | `0` | | [empty-graphemes](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/empty-graphemes.xpath) | `0` | | [entity-name](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/entity-name.xpath) | `á` | | [multi-codepoint-entity](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/multi-codepoint-entity.xpath) | `2` | | [invalid-pad-side](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/invalid-pad-side.xpath) | `FORG0001` | | [empty-padding](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/empty-padding.xpath) | `FORG0001` | | [invalid-trim-side](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/invalid-trim-side.xpath) | `FORG0001` | | [unknown-entity](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/unknown-entity.xpath) | `FOCH0005` | | [surrogate](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/surrogate.xpath) | `FOCH0005` | | [nonstring-characters](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/nonstring-characters.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | The 3.1 output deliberately excludes grapheme count; it verifies the same cleanup, codepoint padding and separator. NBSP is reported as codepoint 160 so an invisible preserved character is reviewable. The ZWJ case supplies woman + joiner + laptop via codepoints. Invalid values verify documented diagnostics. ## 14. Performance Text segmentation and padding process and materialize the supplied text. No display measurement or byte encoding occurs. Very large inputs and padding targets require memory; no benchmark or allocation-free claim is implied. ## 15. Known Uses This customer import is synthetic. Existing evidence includes [`TrimSpace_DefaultTrimsBothEnds`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`TrimSpace_XmlWhitespaceOnly`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PadString_NeverTruncates`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PadString_BothSidesSplitsWithExtraAtEnd`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Characters_NonAsciiString_SplitsByCodepoint`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Graphemes_CombiningMark_AttachesToBase`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Graphemes_EmojiZwjSequence_IsOneGrapheme`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`Char_MultiCodepointEntity_ReturnsFullString`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exact fn-characters to GatedSets. No exact char/graphemes/pad-string/trim-space assignment is claimed. These 22 executable cases provide separate evidence; no gate is promoted. ## 16. Related Features [Import file names](import-file-names.md) covers codepoint substring positions. [Configured label callbacks](configured-label-callbacks.md) covers reusable formatting policies. [The audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) records the grapheme limitation separately from reference-name coverage.

sections.13:
Complete synthetic input; the name contains e followed by combining acute, two interior spaces and a truck emoji:

```xml
<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>
```

### Complete XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $name := string(parse-xml('<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>')/customer/name)
let $label := trim-space($name)
return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(characters($label)), '; graphemes=', count(graphemes($label)), '; export=[', pad-string($label, 10, map {'padding': '.'}), ']; separator=', char(8212))
```

Exact output:

```text
label=[José  🚚]; codepoints=8; graphemes=7; export=[José  🚚..]; separator=—
```

### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $name := string(parse-xml('<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>')/customer/name)
return let $label := replace(replace($name, '^\s+', ''), '\s+$', '')
return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(string-to-codepoints($label)), '; export=[', $label, string-join(for $i in 1 to max((0, 10 - string-length($label))) return '.', ''), ']; separator=', codepoints-to-string(8212))
```

Exact output:

```text
label=[José  🚚]; codepoints=8; export=[José  🚚..]; separator=—
```

functions/element-to-map.md.text:
Element-to-map conversion

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Element-to-map conversion** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:element-to-map](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-element-to-map), [fn:element-to-map-plan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-element-to-map-plan). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #106](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/106), [immutable mainline revision `1bb73147`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/1bb731474c6ba48dded66441183c676a0ebf9761) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Describe the conversion shape explicitly before passing data into a map-oriented pipeline. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, construct the desired map explicitly from XML selectors. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/element-to-map/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/element-to-map/main.xpath). Both yield `FILTER-A` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation An integration adapter needs an XML product code as a map field. Describe the conversion shape explicitly before passing data into a map-oriented pipeline. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Layout and typing options matter for attributes and repeated children. This example deliberately uses a single simple-content element. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Layout and typing options matter for attributes and repeated children. This example deliberately uses a single simple-content element. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:element-to-map(parse-xml('FILTER-A')/sku)?sku ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. functions/higher-order-selection.md.text:
Higher-order selection

Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Higher-order selection — Frozen 4.0.** [Bosak PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88) / [immutable revision `0a928bb8`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790). This is the shipped engine delivery. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:some](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-some), [fn:every](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-every), [fn:index-where](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-index-where). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Validate order lines and locate every rejected line without losing its original position. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 offers `some ... satisfies` and `every ... satisfies` quantified expressions. Positional `for` expressions can locate failures, as the linked baseline demonstrates. Function forms make the predicate a reusable function item; neither syntax nor callback contracts are interchangeable automatically. some/every test whether any/all items satisfy a predicate; index-where returns one-based matching positions. The two-argument callbacks receive item and position. Empty predicate results mean false; arbitrary nonboolean callback results are errors. Empty input gives some=false, every=true and no positions. An explicit existence check is needed when an empty order is invalid. ## 5. Motivation Validate order lines and locate every rejected line without losing its original position. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Do not confuse fn:some/fn:every function calls with the XPath 3.1 quantified-expression grammar. Callback positions refer to the input sequence, not document sibling positions. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer opts into XPath40 and needs the exact validation or ordering contract described here. Keep the XPath 3.1 baseline when that opt-in is unavailable. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(index-where((2, 0, 3), function($quantity, $position) { $quantity le 0 }) ! string(.), ',') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences some/every test whether any/all items satisfy a predicate; index-where returns one-based matching positions. The two-argument callbacks receive item and position. Empty predicate results mean false; arbitrary nonboolean callback results are errors. Empty input gives some=false, every=true and no positions. An explicit existence check is needed when an empty order is invalid. Do not confuse fn:some/fn:every function calls with the XPath 3.1 quantified-expression grammar. Callback positions refer to the input sequence, not document sibling positions. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Any/all/position selection and vacuous empty results; Item and one-based position callbacks; Boolean/empty result conversion and invalid callback arity. **Boundaries:** Callable/subtyping combinations beyond the verified signatures remain unsupported in this consumer reference. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Comparison/selection review](../SELECTION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed warehouse README](../examples/selection-contracts/README.md) supply 68 checks: keyword modes, collation/default/key/predicate, atomization, result/cardinality boundaries and complete 3.1/4.0 reports. duplicate-values/highest/lowest keywords remain unavailable; index-where keywords work. Map tolerance and tested extrema NaN results remain explicit engine follow-ups. Extrema return boundary-equal items, not all distinct records sharing its key. Initial delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. ## 13. Sample Code [main.xpath](../examples/higher-order-selection/main.xpath): returns `2` at mode 40. [edge.xpath](../examples/higher-order-selection/edge.xpath): returns `false/true` at mode 40. [before.xpath](../examples/higher-order-selection/before.xpath): returns `2` at mode 31. ## 14. Performance Notes Duplicate checks and index selection may traverse the input; some/every may finish early. Partitioning creates arrays and retains input items. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `higher-order-selection-main`, `higher-order-selection-edge`, `higher-order-selection-before`. [`Some_PositionArgument_IsOneBased`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Every_EmptyInput_ReturnsTrue`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`IndexWhere_ReturnsAscendingPositions`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs) The exact-name sets `fn-some`, `fn-every` and `fn-index-where` are not in the current GatedSets; named unit tests and published examples provide evidence. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

functions/import-array-batches.md.text:
Import batches with arrays

Frozen 4.0 — verified reference contracts

## 1. Name and Classification **Import batches with arrays — Frozen 4.0.** Shipped in [Bosak PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84) at immutable revision [`f7f55b4e`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19). Functions: [array:build](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-build), [array:empty](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-empty), [array:items](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-items), [array:slice](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-slice). Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable. ## 2. Intent Keep every order’s product-code sequence in one array member, select a two-order import batch, and concatenate the lines only at the export boundary. One order can contain several lines without becoming several orders. ## 3. Also Known As Exact spellings are `array:build`, `array:empty`, `array:items` and `array:slice`. No aliases are introduced. `array:items` performs one-level concatenation; `array:flatten` is the recursive alternative. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 uses `fold-left` and `array:append` to construct one member per order, then `array:subarray` for the illustrated forward batch and `?*` for one-level concatenation. `array:subarray` is not a general substitute for negative bounds, reverse slices, strides or forgiving out-of-range selection. ## 5. Motivation Flattening line sequences before batching destroys order boundaries. Building one array member per callback invocation preserves them even when a callback returns several items or the empty sequence. ## 6. Language Alignment Array members can be arbitrary XPath sequences, unlike a simple list of scalar JSON values. Addresses are one-based. Slice end positions are inclusive, unlike Python and JavaScript slices; negative values count from the end. `array:items` concatenates one level and retains nested arrays, while `array:flatten` is recursive. ## 7. Applicability Use for bounded selections from an already materialized batch. `array:empty([()])` is false: there is one member even though it contains no items. Distinguish no orders from an order with no lines, and validate that business condition separately. ## 8. Structure ```xquery array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines}) array:slice($members, $start, $end, $step) array:empty($members) array:items($members) ``` Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option. ## 9. Participants Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. ## 10. Collaborations The map family indexes products while this array family preserves order boundaries. The [sequence-selection family](order-sequence-selection.md) uses the same slice position rules for ordinary sequences. ## 11. Consequences Each callback result is one array member. `array:items` loses those boundaries, so call it only when flattening one level is intended. `[]`, `[()]` and `[[]]` have different member counts. Empty bounds or zero select defaults; a negative step defaults the omitted start/end to opposite sequence ends. An omitted/zero step chooses direction from the resolved bounds. An explicit incompatible direction returns an empty array, and out-of-range bounds do not raise the `array:subarray` bounds error. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles One callback result per member and one-level item concatenation; Zero members versus empty/nested members; Inclusive/negative slice bounds, default/zero step and empty direction result. **Boundaries:** array:members/of-members are JNode functions owned by C05, not replacements for member/item concatenation. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Implementation: [FunctionLibrary.cs](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); [named unit tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Names refuse XPST0017 in default XPath31; the comparisons remain valid at XPath31. Source/package version stays 1.1.1. This reference work changes no engine code. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Container review](../CONTAINER-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed stock-feed README](../examples/container-contracts/README.md) supply 89 checks covering six families: keyword modes, empty/default/member/item shapes, nested values, node identity, callback arity/results and complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. map:filter boolean-result enforcement remains an engine follow-up. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate evidence and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. The map result-shape corrections already shipped in 1.1.2. ## 13. Sample Code Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. Outputs are exact text projections of XDM results, not serialized supplier or ERP formats. **Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/main.xpath) ```xquery (: One array member holds all product codes for one order. :) let $orders := (map{'id':'ORD-101','lines':('FILTER-A','SEAL-B')}, map{'id':'ORD-102','lines':('VALVE-C')}, map{'id':'ORD-103','lines':('HOSE-D','CLIP-E')}), $members := array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines}), $batch := array:slice($members, 1, 2) return concat('orders=', array:size($batch), ';lines=', string-join(array:items($batch), ',')) ``` Expected text: ```text orders=2;lines=FILTER-A,SEAL-B,VALVE-C ``` **Baseline — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/baseline.xpath) ```xquery let $orders := (map{'id':'ORD-101','lines':('FILTER-A','SEAL-B')}, map{'id':'ORD-102','lines':('VALVE-C')}, map{'id':'ORD-103','lines':('HOSE-D','CLIP-E')}), $members := fold-left($orders, **Import batches with arrays — Frozen 4.0.** Shipped in [Bosak PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84) at immutable revision [`f7f55b4e`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19).

Functions: [array:build](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-build), [array:empty](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-empty), [array:items](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-items), [array:slice](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-slice). Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable.
sections.2: Keep every order’s product-code sequence in one array member, select a two-order import batch, and concatenate the lines only at the export boundary. One order can contain several lines without becoming several orders.
sections.3: Exact spellings are `array:build`, `array:empty`, `array:items` and `array:slice`. No aliases are introduced. `array:items` performs one-level concatenation; `array:flatten` is the recursive alternative.
sections.4: XPath 3.1 uses `fold-left` and `array:append` to construct one member per order, then `array:subarray` for the illustrated forward batch and `?*` for one-level concatenation. `array:subarray` is not a general substitute for negative bounds, reverse slices, strides or forgiving out-of-range selection.
sections.5: Flattening line sequences before batching destroys order boundaries. Building one array member per callback invocation preserves them even when a callback returns several items or the empty sequence.
sections.6: Array members can be arbitrary XPath sequences, unlike a simple list of scalar JSON values. Addresses are one-based. Slice end positions are inclusive, unlike Python and JavaScript slices; negative values count from the end. `array:items` concatenates one level and retains nested arrays, while `array:flatten` is recursive.
sections.7: Use for bounded selections from an already materialized batch. `array:empty([()])` is false: there is one member even though it contains no items. Distinguish no orders from an order with no lines, and validate that business condition separately.
sections.8:
```xquery
array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines})
array:slice($members, $start, $end, $step)
array:empty($members)
array:items($members)
```

Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option.
sections.9: Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms.
sections.10: The map family indexes products while this array family preserves order boundaries. The [sequence-selection family](order-sequence-selection.md) uses the same slice position rules for ordinary sequences.
sections.11: Each callback result is one array member. `array:items` loses those boundaries, so call it only when flattening one level is intended. `[]`, `[()]` and `[[]]` have different member counts. Empty bounds or zero select defaults; a negative step defaults the omitted start/end to opposite sequence ends. An omitted/zero step chooses direction from the resolved bounds. An explicit incompatible direction returns an empty array, and out-of-range bounds do not raise the `array:subarray` bounds error.

functions/import-file-names.md.text:
Import File Names

Frozen 4.0 — real-world import text contracts

## 1. Name and Classification **Import file names — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:substring-before-last](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-substring-before-last), [fn:substring-after-last](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-substring-after-last), and [fn:index-of-substring](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-index-of-substring). Initial delivery: [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39), REQ-118 S1 part 2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-12** against immutable [QT4CG source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). The eight reviewed function definitions are unchanged from the earlier a014e1b4 review pin. This does not recover unavailable historical adopted specification snapshots. ## 2. Intent Split an import path at its final slash and a file name at its final dot, preserving earlier dots. Report dot positions to make the chosen extension boundary explicit. ## 3. Also Known As Last-delimiter extraction and substring-position search are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can enumerate matching codepoint positions, select the last one and slice with substring. The complete comparison implements the illustrated slash/dot contract. It is scoped to this path with present delimiters; a general helper must also handle missing and empty delimiters explicitly. ## 5. Motivation An import directory can contain dots and a file can have multiple suffixes. Splitting at the first dot would mistake invoice.batch.xml for extension batch.xml. A final-boundary rule gives stem invoice.batch and extension xml, matching the stated importer policy. ## 6. Language Alignment Last-substring functions return the parts before or after the last match under the chosen collation. If no match exists, both return an empty string. With an empty delimiter, before-last returns the input and after-last returns empty. They accept an optional collation; the case uses the default codepoint collation. index-of-substring reports one-based codepoint positions, includes overlapping matches, and has no collation argument. An empty substring matches each boundary through length+1. Empty source with a nonempty needle produces no positions; an empty source and empty needle produce one boundary. These are codepoint positions, not UTF-16 storage indices or grapheme-cluster indices. ## 7. Applicability Use for a declared lexical slash/dot import convention. The main fixture assumes a nonempty slash-separated path with a final filename and a dot extension. It does not access files, normalize Windows paths, parse URIs or classify compound archives. For archive.tar.gz the final extension is gz; recognizing tar.gz as a compound format requires a separate policy. URI percent escapes and query/fragment boundaries belong to [URI component parsing](invoice-api-uris.md). ## 8. Structure Select the text path, derive directory and final filename, then derive stem/extension and all dot positions from that filename. Dots in the directory do not affect extension selection. ## 9. Participants The file record supplies text. Last-match functions select boundaries. Position search exposes filename delimiters. The report shows the exact import classification. ## 10. Collaborations Extract the filename before searching its dots. Apply presence guards in a production importer if a missing delimiter must preserve the whole filename rather than produce empty. Use an explicit collation for case-insensitive text delimiters; the index function remains codepoint matching. ## 11. Consequences Earlier separators and dots remain in the preceding parts. Overlapping delimiters can select a later start than a non-overlapping tokenizer would. No delimiter is an empty-result contract, not an automatic whole-filename fallback. No path authorization or file operation occurs. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Last delimiter, overlap and one-based codepoint positions; Empty needle/source, default collation and malformed collation; Experimental absent-pattern correction with frozen refusal retained. **Boundaries:** Do not rely on tolerated typed-numeric string arguments; no grapheme-position or path-authorization contract. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use CompileOptions.Compatibility40 for the new calls and Compatibility31 for the comparison. Default 3.1 rejects new names. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact report/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All inputs are inline. **Supplementary text-contract review (2026-10-12):** [Eight-family contract review](../TEXT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed label/filename README](../examples/text-contracts/README.md) supply explicit keyword refusals at 3.1/4.0/experimental, positional defaults/empty/invalid cases and complete paired reports. Numeric substring/option tolerance and validation boundaries remain observed follow-ups; the review does not implement keywords or certify full Unicode/coercion conformance. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic file record: ```xml ``` ### Complete XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/main.xpath): ```xpath let $path := string(parse-xml('')/file/@path) let $directory := substring-before-last($path, '/') let $name := substring-after-last($path, '/') return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring-before-last($name, '.'), '; extension=', substring-after-last($name, '.'), '; dots=', string-join(index-of-substring($name, '.') ! string(.), ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14 ``` ### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison [Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $path := string(parse-xml('')/file/@path) return let $positions := function($value, $needle) { for $p in 1 to string-length($value) return if (substring($value, $p, string-length($needle)) eq $needle) then $p else () } return let $slash := $positions($path, '/')[last()] return let $directory := substring($path, 1, $slash - 1) return let $name := substring($path, $slash + 1) return let $dots := $positions($name, '.') return let $dot := $dots[last()] return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring($name, 1, $dot - 1), '; extension=', substring($name, $dot + 1), '; dots=', string-join($dots ! string(.), ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14 ``` ### Boundary and error inventory Each file embeds its complete input. Brackets make significant spaces visible. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/import-file-names/main.xpath) | `directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14` | | [baseline](../examples/import-file-names/baseline.xpath) | `directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14` | | [compound-extension](../examples/import-file-names/compound-extension.xpath) | `gz` | | [missing-delimiter](../examples/import-file-names/missing-delimiter.xpath) | `[]|[]` | | [empty-delimiter](../examples/import-file-names/empty-delimiter.xpath) | `[invoice]|[]` | | [overlapping](../examples/import-file-names/overlapping.xpath) | `before=a; after=[]; positions=1,2` | | [no-matches](../examples/import-file-names/no-matches.xpath) | `0` | | [empty-search](../examples/import-file-names/empty-search.xpath) | `1,2,3,4` | | [empty-source](../examples/import-file-names/empty-source.xpath) | `0` | | [empty-both](../examples/import-file-names/empty-both.xpath) | `[]|[]` | | [supplementary-position](../examples/import-file-names/supplementary-position.xpath) | `1,3` | | [explicit-collation](../examples/import-file-names/explicit-collation.xpath) | `-c` | | [multi-item-source](../examples/import-file-names/multi-item-source.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | The overlapping fixture reports matches at positions one and two in aaa for aa. Supplementary-character positions verify codepoints. The case-insensitive collation fixture tests a textual delimiter separately from the path rule. Missing/empty delimiters and empty source inputs are distinct cases. ## 14. Performance Position search materializes match positions and text extraction works on supplied strings. The 3.1 comparison scans candidate positions explicitly. No benchmark, filesystem access or universal complexity claim follows. ## 15. Known Uses **Experimental empty-argument correction (source1.24.1):** [Contract](../INDEX-OF-SUBSTRING-CONTRACT.md), [38 public API controls](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/SubstringExperimentalContractTests.cs) and [two host controls](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/SubstringExperimentalHostBoundaryTests.cs) verify the newer absent-pattern result only under `XPath40Experimental`. Frozen `fn-index-of-substring` case021 still requires XPTY0004; current upstream case021 remains a diagnostic failure in the frozen runner. No current-gate promotion or historical provenance recovery is claimed. This importer rule is synthetic. Existing evidence includes [`IndexOfSubstring_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`IndexOfSubstring_EmptySubstring_MatchesEveryPosition`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`IndexOfSubstring_PositionsInCodepoints`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`SubstringBeforeLast_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`SubstringAfterLast_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`SubstringAfterLast_WithCollation`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exact fn-index-of-substring to GatedSets. No exact before-last/after-last assignment is claimed. These 13 executable cases provide separate evidence. Gate membership is unchanged. ## 16. Related Features [Customer text cleanup](customer-text-cleanup.md) distinguishes codepoints and supported grapheme clusters. [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md) handles URI boundaries. [The audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) separates reference coverage from exhaustive collation/signature conformance.

sections.13:
Complete synthetic file record:

```xml
<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>
```

### Complete XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $path := string(parse-xml('<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>')/file/@path)
let $directory := substring-before-last($path, '/')
let $name := substring-after-last($path, '/')
return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring-before-last($name, '.'), '; extension=', substring-after-last($name, '.'), '; dots=', string-join(index-of-substring($name, '.') ! string(.), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14
```

### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $path := string(parse-xml('<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>')/file/@path)
return let $positions := function($value, $needle) { for $p in 1 to string-length($value) return if (substring($value, $p, string-length($needle)) eq $needle) then $p else () }
return let $slash := $positions($path, '/')[last()]
return let $directory := substring($path, 1, $slash - 1)
return let $name := substring($path, $slash + 1)
return let $dots := $positions($name, '.')
return let $dot := $dots[last()]
return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring($name, 1, $dot - 1), '; extension=', substring($name, $dot + 1), '; dots=', string-join($dots ! string(.), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14
```

functions/invoice-api-uris.md.text:
Invoice API URIs

Frozen 4.0 — parse components, build routes and decode values

## 1. Name and Classification **Invoice API URIs — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:parse-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-parse-uri), [fn:build-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-build-uri), and [fn:decode-from-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-decode-from-uri). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. General syntax references: [RFC 3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) and [RFC 3987](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3987). The pinned function draft also specifies convenient handling for some URI-adjacent strings. ## 2. Intent Construct an invoice API route from a configured endpoint, an invoice identifier and a search value. Preserve a slash inside the identifier as data in one path segment and distinguish a literal plus from a query-parameter space. ## 3. Also Known As URI decomposition, component assembly and percent decoding are descriptive terms. No aliases are registered. Form decoding is a distinct convention used for query parameters, not a synonym for generic URI decoding. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can assemble a fixed route with `concat` and `encode-for-uri` on each identifier/query value. The complete comparison below constructs the same URI for this configured HTTPS `/v1` endpoint. Its explicit removal of port 443 is scoped to that fixture, not a general-purpose URI parser. XPath 3.1 has no direct standard counterpart to the complete component-record parser or UTF-8 percent decoder; a host implementation or dedicated helper is needed for general decoding. ## 5. Motivation An invoice ID such as INV/2048 may contain a slash as part of its business key. Concatenating it into the route without segment encoding creates two route segments. Likewise, a plus in a search value must not turn into a space when the server form-decodes query parameters. Component-based assembly makes those boundaries explicit before the host uses the resulting address. ## 6. Language Alignment `parse-uri` returns an optional map with raw and derived fields, including scheme, host, integer port, path, decoded path-segments, query, decoded query-parameters and fragment. Repeated query keys collect a sequence of values. Parsing query parameters applies form decoding: plus becomes space before percent decoding. An encoded `%2B` becomes a literal plus. Empty input returns empty. `build-uri` takes a component map. Nonempty path-segments take precedence over path in the demonstrated cases; a nonempty query-parameters map takes precedence over query. A leading empty segment supplies the initial slash. Each hierarchical segment is encoded independently, so a slash inside a segment becomes `%2F`. Query values use their own delimiter-encoding rules. Non-hierarchical schemes such as mailto have different assembly rules; this entry's business route is HTTPS. `decode-from-uri` percent-decodes UTF-8 and leaves ordinary plus signs unchanged. Empty input becomes a zero-length string, unlike parse-uri's empty result. Malformed escapes, invalid UTF-8 and XML-invalid characters become U+FFFD replacement characters in the specified cases, rather than throwing a strict validation error. Do not decode the entire address before identifying its boundaries. The functions have optional options maps for parsing/building. This case uses `omit-default-ports` to omit HTTPS port 443; a nondefault port is preserved. The entry verifies that option and default behavior, not every option/signature. ## 7. Applicability Use for component-aware integration addresses and decoded values. The fixture assumes a validated HTTPS endpoint with the known `/v1` route, a nonempty invoice ID, and a supplied search value. The parser accepts relative references and URI-adjacent strings; successful parsing is not proof that an address is an approved API endpoint or a valid network destination. The host owns endpoint validation, relative-reference resolution and actual network requests. Do not infer a canonical signed-request spelling from a parse/build roundtrip. Keep original wire text when a protocol requires its exact bytes or query order. Generic decoding is permissive and may lose malformed input through replacement. ## 8. Structure Read the request, parse its base endpoint with default-port omission, then build scheme/host/port, separate route segments and a one-key query map. Parse the built URI to verify that invoice ID and search text still have their original values. No HTTP operation is performed. ## 9. Participants The request supplies endpoint and business values. The parser exposes endpoint components. The builder escapes component data and joins delimiters. The parsed result and report demonstrate the roundtrip of the business values. ## 10. Collaborations Pass raw component values to path-segments/query-parameters; do not pre-escape them and then ask the builder to escape again. The fixed 3.1 comparison instead calls `encode-for-uri` before concatenating delimiters. The decoder is useful for a component already isolated from its address; query form handling requires the plus-to-space step first. The form-decoding fixture illustrates that order. ## 11. Consequences Slash, space, question mark, hash and plus are preserved as component data in the verified cases. Parsing/building may change spelling: spaces become escaped, query plus may rebuild as `%20`, and configured default ports may disappear. Repeated query values remain sequences; map iteration does not promise a portable query-key order. The exact builder fixtures use one query key so they do not imply such an ordering contract. Semantic value preservation differs from byte-for-byte roundtripping. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Raw and decoded URI fields, repeated query keys and plus/percent behavior; Structured segment/query precedence and non-byte-preserving roundtrip; One-pass UTF-8 decoding, absence and malformed syntax. **Boundaries:** Use validated typed Boolean options and remove raw query when deliberately supplying an empty query map. Follow-up groups: F01, F04. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for the new functions. The default XPath 3.1 profile rejects them. The fixed route comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact results/errors and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All inputs are inline, and the example hostname is illustrative. No external context item, variables, files or HTTP request are required. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [URI/import utility review](../URI-UTILITY-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed import/link README](../examples/utility-contracts/README.md) supply 105 checks across five families: keyword modes, component/options/escaping, one-pass UTF-8 decoding, collation availability, identity, NaN and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Boolean-option/record tolerance and empty query-map precedence remain follow-ups. All 37 absent-keyword families now have first targeted review, with metadata still absent; this does not close D2. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/invoice-api-uris/main.xpath): ```xpath let $request := parse-xml('')/request let $base := parse-uri(string($request/@endpoint), map {'omit-default-ports': true()}) let $uri := build-uri(map {'scheme': $base?scheme, 'host': $base?host, 'port': $base?port, 'path-segments': ('', 'v1', 'invoices', string($request/@invoice)), 'query-parameters': map {'q': string($request/@query)}}) let $parsed := parse-uri($uri) return concat('uri=', $uri, '; invoice=', $parsed?path-segments[4], '; query=', $parsed?query-parameters?q) ``` Exact output: ```text uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV/2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 construction comparison](../examples/invoice-api-uris/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $request := parse-xml('')/request return let $origin := replace(substring-before(string($request/@endpoint), '/v1'), ':443$', '') return let $uri := concat($origin, '/v1/invoices/', encode-for-uri(string($request/@invoice)), '?q=', encode-for-uri(string($request/@query))) return $uri ``` Exact output (URI construction only): ```text https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT ``` ### Delimiters inside the identifier Full input contains both a question mark and a hash in the invoice ID: ```xml ``` The [delimiter fixture](../examples/invoice-api-uris/delimiter-in-id.xpath) reports: ```text uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%3F2048%23A?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV?2048#A; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each file embeds its full input and exact result or diagnostic marker. `�` below is the literal Unicode replacement character U+FFFD. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/invoice-api-uris/main.xpath) | `uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV/2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT` | | [baseline](../examples/invoice-api-uris/baseline.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT` | | [space-in-id](../examples/invoice-api-uris/space-in-id.xpath) | `uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%202048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV 2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT` | | [delimiter-in-id](../examples/invoice-api-uris/delimiter-in-id.xpath) | `uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%3F2048%23A?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV?2048#A; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT` | | [duplicate-query](../examples/invoice-api-uris/duplicate-query.xpath) | `ready,review` | | [build-duplicate-query](../examples/invoice-api-uris/build-duplicate-query.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/?tag=ready&tag=review` | | [query-plus](../examples/invoice-api-uris/query-plus.xpath) | `Ada Lovelace` | | [literal-plus](../examples/invoice-api-uris/literal-plus.xpath) | `Ada+Lovelace` | | [decode-plus](../examples/invoice-api-uris/decode-plus.xpath) | `Ada+Lovelace` | | [decode-form](../examples/invoice-api-uris/decode-form.xpath) | `Ada Lovelace+` | | [decode-utf8](../examples/invoice-api-uris/decode-utf8.xpath) | `café` | | [encode-decode](../examples/invoice-api-uris/encode-decode.xpath) | `INV/2048 + VAT` | | [malformed-escape](../examples/invoice-api-uris/malformed-escape.xpath) | `�!` | | [invalid-utf8](../examples/invoice-api-uris/invalid-utf8.xpath) | `�A` | | [decode-empty](../examples/invoice-api-uris/decode-empty.xpath) | `0` | | [parse-empty](../examples/invoice-api-uris/parse-empty.xpath) | `0` | | [default-port](../examples/invoice-api-uris/default-port.xpath) | `0` | | [custom-port](../examples/invoice-api-uris/custom-port.xpath) | `8443` | | [port-type](../examples/invoice-api-uris/port-type.xpath) | `true` | | [relative-reference](../examples/invoice-api-uris/relative-reference.xpath) | `scheme=false; path=../invoices/INV2048; query=ready` | | [fragment-only](../examples/invoice-api-uris/fragment-only.xpath) | `pathCount=0; fragment=summary view` | | [ipv6-host](../examples/invoice-api-uris/ipv6-host.xpath) | `[2001:db8::7]` | | [normalized-roundtrip](../examples/invoice-api-uris/normalized-roundtrip.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/p%20x?q=Ada%20Lovelace#summary%20view` | | [segment-precedence](../examples/invoice-api-uris/segment-precedence.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/invoices/INV%2F2048` | | [query-precedence](../examples/invoice-api-uris/query-precedence.xpath) | `https://api.example.test?q=ready` | | [nonhierarchical](../examples/invoice-api-uris/nonhierarchical.xpath) | `mailto:accounts@example.test` | | [unmatched-ipv6](../examples/invoice-api-uris/unmatched-ipv6.xpath) | `FOUR0001` | | [build-nonmap](../examples/invoice-api-uris/build-nonmap.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | The duplicate-key fixtures parse and rebuild ready/review tags in one key's value sequence. Plus fixtures distinguish raw plus, encoded plus, generic percent decoding and query form decoding. UTF-8 and malformed-input fixtures verify decoding behavior. Relative/fragment references demonstrate that parsing alone does not establish an absolute API address. Port and IPv6 fixtures verify component types and authority structure. Precedence and normalized-roundtrip fixtures explain how assembly chooses fields and changes textual spelling. ## 14. Performance Parsing and assembly process supplied strings and component values synchronously. Repeated query keys create sequence-valued map entries. These functions do not resolve DNS, access files or fetch resources. No benchmark or universal complexity claim is implied; large inputs still require memory for component strings/maps. ## 15. Known Uses This invoice API route is a synthetic integration example. Existing evidence includes [`ParseUri_HierarchicalHttp_AllFields`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`ParseUri_PortIsInteger`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`ParseUri_QueryParametersAccumulateDuplicateKeys`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`ParseUri_OmitDefaultPorts`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`ParseUri_UnmatchedBracketInAuthority_RaisesFour0001`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildUri_ParseRoundTrip_ReencodesDelimiters`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildUri_PathSegmentsEscapedOnlyWhenHierarchical`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildUri_QueryParameters_EscapeAndEmptyKey`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DecodeFromUri_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`DecodeFromUri_InvalidEscapesAndInvalidUtf8_BecomeReplacementChar`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) has no exact fn-parse-uri, fn-build-uri or fn-decode-from-uri assignment in GatedSets. Named tests and these 28 executable examples provide separate evidence. No gate membership changes are included. ## 16. Related Features [Archive and partner URI policy](uri-option-policy.md) extends this reference with Boolean option contracts, UNC interpretation and raw/structured component precedence, including observed option-validation and empty-query-map limits. [Configured label callbacks](configured-label-callbacks.md) covers reusable configuration values. [Timestamp deadlines](timestamp-deadlines.md) covers other integration-unit conversions. sections.9:
The request supplies endpoint and business values. The parser exposes endpoint
components. The builder escapes component data and joins delimiters. The parsed
result and report demonstrate the roundtrip of the business values.
sections.10:
Pass raw component values to path-segments/query-parameters; do not pre-escape
them and then ask the builder to escape again. The fixed 3.1 comparison instead
calls `encode-for-uri` before concatenating delimiters. The decoder is useful
for a component already isolated from its address; query form handling requires
the plus-to-space step first. The form-decoding fixture illustrates that order.
sections.11:
Slash, space, question mark, hash and plus are preserved as component data in
the verified cases. Parsing/building may change spelling: spaces become escaped,
query plus may rebuild as `%20`, and configured default ports may disappear.
Repeated query values remain sequences; map iteration does not promise a
portable query-key order. The exact builder fixtures use one query key so they
do not imply such an ordering contract. Semantic value preservation differs
from byte-for-byte roundtripping.
sections.12:
**C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Raw and decoded URI fields, repeated query keys and plus/percent behavior; Structured segment/query precedence and non-byte-preserving roundtrip; One-pass UTF-8 decoding, absence and malformed syntax. **Boundaries:** Use validated typed Boolean options and remove raw query when deliberately supplying an empty query map. Follow-up groups: F01, F04. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance.

Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for the new functions. The default XPath
3.1 profile rejects them. The fixed route comparison uses `Compatibility31`.
The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs)
checks exact results/errors and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases.
All inputs are inline, and the example hostname is illustrative. No external
context item, variables, files or HTTP request are required.

**Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [URI/import utility review](../URI-UTILITY-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed import/link README](../examples/utility-contracts/README.md) supply 105 checks across five families: keyword modes, component/options/escaping, one-pass UTF-8 decoding, collation availability, identity, NaN and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Boolean-option/record tolerance and empty query-map precedence remain follow-ups. All 37 absent-keyword families now have first targeted review, with metadata still absent; this does not close D2. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain.
sections.13:
Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<request endpoint="https://api.example.test:443/v1" invoice="INV/2048" query="Ada Lovelace + VAT"/>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/invoice-api-uris/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $request := parse-xml('<request endpoint="https://api.example.test:443/v1" invoice="INV/2048" query="Ada Lovelace + VAT"/>')/request
let $base := parse-uri(string($request/@endpoint), map {'omit-default-ports': true()})
let $uri := build-uri(map {'scheme': $base?scheme, 'host': $base?host, 'port': $base?port, 'path-segments': ('', 'v1', 'invoices', string($request/@invoice)), 'query-parameters': map {'q': string($request/@query)}})
let $parsed := parse-uri($uri)
return concat('uri=', $uri, '; invoice=', $parsed?path-segments[4], '; query=', $parsed?query-parameters?q)
```

Exact output:

```text
uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV/2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 construction comparison](../examples/invoice-api-uris/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $request := parse-xml('<request endpoint="https://api.example.test:443/v1" invoice="INV/2048" query="Ada Lovelace + VAT"/>')/request
return let $origin := replace(substring-before(string($request/@endpoint), '/v1'), ':443$', '')
return let $uri := concat($origin, '/v1/invoices/', encode-for-uri(string($request/@invoice)), '?q=', encode-for-uri(string($request/@query)))
return $uri
```

Exact output (URI construction only):

```text
https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT
```

### Delimiters inside the identifier

Full input contains both a question mark and a hash in the invoice ID:

```xml
<request endpoint="https://api.example.test:443/v1" invoice="INV?2048#A" query="Ada Lovelace + VAT"/>
```

The [delimiter fixture](../examples/invoice-api-uris/delimiter-in-id.xpath) reports:

```text
uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%3F2048%23A?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV?2048#A; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT
```

value sequence. Plus fixtures distinguish raw plus, encoded plus, generic
percent decoding and query form decoding. UTF-8 and malformed-input fixtures
verify decoding behavior. Relative/fragment references demonstrate that parsing
alone does not establish an absolute API address. Port and IPv6 fixtures verify
component types and authority structure. Precedence and normalized-roundtrip
fixtures explain how assembly chooses fields and changes textual spelling.

Parsing and assembly process supplied strings and component values synchronously.
Repeated query keys create sequence-valued map entries. These functions do not
resolve DNS, access files or fetch resources. No benchmark or universal complexity
claim is implied; large inputs still require memory for component strings/maps.

functions/map-to-element.md.text:
Map-to-element conversion

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Map-to-element conversion** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:map-to-element](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-map-to-element). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #106](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/106), [immutable mainline revision `1bb73147`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/1bb731474c6ba48dded66441183c676a0ebf9761) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Convert an agreed map shape back into XML and inspect its text value. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, an XSLT template or XQuery constructor builds the target XML explicitly. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/map-to-element/before.xsl) with the [complete expression](../examples/map-to-element/main.xpath). Both yield `FILTER-A` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A map-based integration step must deliver a small XML product element. Convert an agreed map shape back into XML and inspect its text value. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. A conversion is not automatically a lossless round trip for arbitrary mixed-content XML; agree on namespaces and layout. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. A conversion is not automatically a lossless round trip for arbitrary mixed-content XML; agree on namespaces and layout. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string(fn:map-to-element(map { 'sku': 'FILTER-A' })) ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Convert an agreed map shape back into XML and inspect its text value. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. A conversion is not automatically a lossless round trip for arbitrary mixed-content XML; agree on namespaces and layout. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Single tested map-to-XML conversion shape; QName/name/layout, nested content and option boundaries are distinct. **Boundaries:** The reduced example does not certify the whole conversion-plan/record/namespaces space; supplementary provider Unicode limits belong to the deferred skip queue. Current-draft escape-names encoding is unsupported; use XML-compatible field names and verified conversion options. Follow-up groups: F01, F14. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** Keyword drift: implemented input differs from pinned map; the [signature audit](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) publishes paired success/refusal files. Positional conversion remains separate evidence. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/map-to-element/main.xpath) yields `FILTER-A`. The [edge case](../examples/map-to-element/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: output-size dependent construction. The resulting element tree occupies memory in addition to its source map. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `map-to-element-main`, `map-to-element-edge`, `map-to-element-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`MapToElement_SingleEntryMap_BuildsElement`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs), [`MapToElement_EmptySequence_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs), [`MapToElement_NonMapInput_Xpty0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs). Named frozen gate: `fn-map-to-element`, enforced after the [gate-name repair](../MAP-TO-ELEMENT-GATE-REPAIR.md). The native set contributes156 passed /0 failed /2 skipped; the complete expanded gate passes8,434/0/1,896. Synthetic controls verify that a failing assertion now causes exit2. This is bounded frozen-revision evidence; current-upstream map/element contract changes remain separate. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

functions/measurement-comparison.md.text:
Typed Measurement Comparison

Frozen 4.0 — a changed existing-function contract

**Related current review:** [Equality/collation contracts](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) refresh the five-family declarations, complete customer example, keyword boundaries and explicitly separate engine findings without replacing the historical evidence below. ## 1. Name and Classification [fn:compare](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-compare) is an existing XPath 3.1 function with expanded 4.0 comparison semantics. It is therefore absent from the 117-name inventory of **4.0-only** functions. Bosak delivery: [PR #112](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/112), [89c90b4d](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/89c90b4d5b6a216a4a37223e169d36e3a1a832bd). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review, not recovery of a historical adoption pin. ## 2. Intent Classify imported measurements relative to declared decimal limits while keeping their supplied numeric types. Show why a binary floating-point reading written as `3.1` can compare above or below the decimal value `3.1`. ## 3. Also Known As Three-way comparison, atomic ordering and mixed numeric comparison describe the operation. There is no new registered function name or alias. ## 4.
