Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>
```

### XPath 4.0 report

[Runnable file](../examples/measurement-comparison/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>')/readings/reading
return string-join(for $row in $rows return
  let $value := if (string($row/@value) = '') then () else
    if ($row/@kind = 'decimal') then xs:decimal($row/@value) else
    if ($row/@kind = 'float') then xs:float($row/@value) else xs:double($row/@value)
  return let $limit := xs:decimal($row/@limit)
  return let $status := if (empty($value) or not($value eq $value)) then 'missing' else
    let $order := compare($value, $limit)
    return if ($order lt 0) then 'below' else if ($order eq 0) then 'at-limit' else 'above'
  return concat($row/@id, '=', $status), ';')
```

Exact output:

```text
A=at-limit;B=above;C=below;D=missing;E=missing
```

A is decimal 2 against decimal 2. B and C share the decimal limit 3.1 but retain
their distinct binary representations. D contains numeric NaN and E has no value;
both are reported as missing instead of being silently ranked below the limit.

[Runnable file](../examples/measurement-comparison/baseline.xpath):

```xpath

return string-join(for $row in $rows return
  let $value := if (string($row/@value) = '') then () else
    if ($row/@kind = 'decimal') then xs:decimal($row/@value) else
    if ($row/@kind = 'float') then xs:float($row/@value) else xs:double($row/@value)
  return let $limit := xs:decimal($row/@limit)
  return let $status := if (empty($value) or not($value eq $value)) then 'missing' else
    let $normalized := xs:double($value)
    return let $boundary := xs:double($limit)
    return if ($normalized lt $boundary) then 'below' else if ($normalized eq $boundary) then 'at-limit' else 'above'
  return concat($row/@id, '=', $status), ';')
```

```text
A=at-limit;B=at-limit;C=below;D=missing;E=missing
```

functions/month-end-cutoffs.md.text:
Month-end Cutoffs

Frozen 4.0 — Gregorian components and explicit timezone offsets

## 1. Name and Classification **Month-end cutoffs — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:build-dateTime](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-build-dateTime) and [fn:days-in-month](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-days-in-month). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Construct the final-day invoice submission cutoff for a given month, local clock time and explicit offset. Show both the local cutoff and its equivalent UTC instant. ## 3. Also Known As Calendar construction and month-length lookup are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. The case is a calendar-month cutoff, not a last-business-day rule. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can find the final date by adding a year-month duration to the first of the month, then subtracting one day. The complete comparison uses `dateTime` to combine that date and a time, then attaches the supplied offset and converts to UTC. Its report matches the 4.0 case; the constructor's result type is not thereby claimed to match the new function's `xs:dateTimeStamp` subtype. ## 5. Motivation Invoice submission calendars may specify a fixed local cutoff on the final day of each month. Hardcoding day 31 fails in shorter months, and February requires the Gregorian century rule. Reporting the UTC instant helps a scheduler consume the local business rule without guessing the offset. ## 6. Language Alignment `days-in-month` accepts an optional `xs:dateTime`, `xs:date` or `xs:gYearMonth`, returning 28, 29, 30 or 31 for its **local** year/month. A value whose UTC instant falls in February may still have a March local month. Leap years are divisible by four, except centuries not divisible by 400. Empty input returns empty. `build-dateTime` constructs a Gregorian value from a component map. Full date and clock components plus timezone produce `xs:dateTimeStamp`; omitting timezone produces `xs:dateTime` without inventing an offset. Date-only fields produce `xs:date`, and clock-only fields produce `xs:time`. Empty input returns empty. Unused components can be absent or empty; arbitrary incomplete field combinations raise FODT0005. Invalid calendar/clock values raise FORG0001; an offset outside ±14 hours raises FODT0003. Midnight uses hour zero, not 24. ## 7. Applicability Use when a rule supplies a calendar month, a local clock time and a numeric UTC offset. This fixture assumes present, valid numeric fields and an explicit whole-minute offset. It does not handle weekends, holidays or business calendars. An offset such as +02:00 is not an IANA timezone and carries no daylight-saving rules; the host must resolve a named zone for the scheduled date before supplying its offset. No implicit timezone or current clock is used here. The subsequent 1.1.3 contract review verifies year-zero date/dateTime and year-10000 date construction, as well as year-zero month-length lookup. These observed forms supersede the earlier blanket construction-limit statement; not every extended-year operation or range is certified. ## 8. Structure Read the schedule, build the first local date, ask for its month length, and build a cutoff on that final day. Convert the already offset-bearing cutoff to UTC with `adjust-dateTime-to-timezone`, preserving its instant. ## 9. Participants Schedule attributes provide year, month, clock and offset. Month-length lookup selects a valid final day. The component constructor creates the cutoff. The UTC projection and report expose the resulting scheduling decision. ## 10. Collaborations The first date has day one so month-length lookup can run before constructing the last date. In the 3.1 comparison, attaching an offset to an unzoned local value establishes its instant; the subsequent UTC conversion preserves that instant. These are two distinct uses of timezone adjustment. ## 11. Consequences The report remains correct for common and leap February and 30-day months. Explicit offsets make both displayed instants deterministic. The function does not silently repair invalid input, derive a timezone from geography, or decide whether the configured cutoff is a working day. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Local Gregorian month/leap rules and supported partial Gregorian values; Timezone presence, field-set, calendar and offset errors; Fractional components and declared singleton/type boundaries. **Boundaries:** Millisecond precision loss, permissive malformed/multi-item input and interop calendar bounds remain explicit; arbitrary extended-year operations are not certified. Follow-up groups: F01, F10. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for the new functions; default XPath 3.1 rejects them. The earlier-version comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact text/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All inputs are inline; no current date, external variables or context item are needed. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Date/time review](../DATE-TIME-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed receipt-retention README](../examples/date-contracts/README.md) supply 108 checks across five families: keywords, Gregorian field sets, offsets, units, empty/default, precision and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Malformed/multi-item tolerance, record conversion and fractional-component loss remain engine follow-ups. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic schedule input: ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/main.xpath): ```xpath let $schedule := parse-xml('')/schedule let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year) let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month) let $days := days-in-month(build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': 1})) let $cutoff := build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': $days, 'hours': xs:integer($schedule/@hours), 'minutes': xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), 'seconds': 0, 'timezone': xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone)}) return concat('days=', $days, '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S'))) ``` Exact output: ```text days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $schedule := parse-xml('')/schedule return let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year) return let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month) return let $first := xs:date(concat(format-integer($year, '0000'), '-', format-integer($month, '00'), '-01')) return let $last := $first + xs:yearMonthDuration('P1M') - xs:dayTimeDuration('P1D') return let $local := dateTime($last, xs:time(concat(format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@hours), '00'), ':', format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), '00'), ':00'))) return let $cutoff := adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($local, xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone)) return concat('days=', day-from-date($last), '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S'))) ``` Exact output: ```text days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z ``` ### Common-year boundary Full input changes the year to 2023: ```xml ``` The [common-year expression](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/common-year.xpath) reports: ```text days=28; cutoff=2023-02-28T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2023-02-28T15:30:00Z ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each linked file contains its full expression and input. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/main.xpath) | `days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z` | | [baseline](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/baseline.xpath) | `days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z` | | [common-year](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/common-year.xpath) | `days=28; cutoff=2023-02-28T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2023-02-28T15:30:00Z` | | [thirty-day-month](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/thirty-day-month.xpath) | `days=30; cutoff=2024-04-30T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-04-30T15:30:00Z` | | [negative-offset](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/negative-offset.xpath) | `days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00-05:00; utc=2024-02-29T22:30:00Z` | | [century-common](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/century-common.xpath) | `28` | | [century-leap](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/century-leap.xpath) | `29` | | [year-zero-month](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/year-zero-month.xpath) | `29` | | [local-month](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/local-month.xpath) | `31` | | [empty-month](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/empty-month.xpath) | `0` | | [empty-build](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/empty-build.xpath) | `0` | | [fractional-time](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/fractional-time.xpath) | `13:30:04.25` | | [date-only](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/date-only.xpath) | `2024-02-29` | | [without-timezone](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/without-timezone.xpath) | `dateTime=true; stamp=false; timezone=false` | | [stamp-type](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/stamp-type.xpath) | `true` | | [invalid-fields](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/invalid-fields.xpath) | `FODT0005` | | [invalid-day](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/invalid-day.xpath) | `FORG0001` | | [invalid-offset](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/invalid-offset.xpath) | `FODT0003` | | [midnight-24](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/midnight-24.xpath) | `FORG0001` | Century cases distinguish 1900 from 2000. The local-month case retains March's 31 days even though its instant is in February UTC. Other cases verify empty inputs, date/time output forms, fractional seconds, stamp versus unzoned type, invalid field sets, calendar dates, timezone offsets and the midnight-hour rule. ## 14. Performance Month-length lookup and fixed component construction are small deterministic operations. There is no network acquisition, timezone-database lookup or scheduling loop. The example parses one small inline record; no benchmark claim is implied. ## 15. Known Uses This invoice-calendar rule is synthetic, not an identified deployment. Existing evidence includes [`DaysInMonth_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DaysInMonth_ProlepticGregorianYearZeroIsLeap`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildDateTime_SpecDateTimeStampExample`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildDateTime_AllSevenComponentsWithoutTimezone_IsDateTime`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildDateTime_TimeWithFractionalSeconds`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildDateTime_InvalidFieldSet_RaisesFodt0005`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`BuildDateTime_TimezoneOutOfRange_RaisesFodt0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`BuildDateTime_OutOfRangeComponent_RaisesForg0001`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) has no exact fn-build-dateTime or fn-days-in-month assignment in GatedSets. Named unit tests and these 19 examples provide separate evidence. No gate is promoted here. ## 16. Related Features [Timestamp deadlines](timestamp-deadlines.md) covers elapsed durations and epoch units. [Bounded retry state](bounded-retries.md) covers attempt budgets rather than calendar instants. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) tracks reference names separately from exhaustive signature conformance.

sections.13:
Complete synthetic schedule input:

```xml
<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $schedule := parse-xml('<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>')/schedule
let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year)
let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month)
let $days := days-in-month(build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': 1}))
let $cutoff := build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': $days, 'hours': xs:integer($schedule/@hours), 'minutes': xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), 'seconds': 0, 'timezone': xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone)})
return concat('days=', $days, '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S')))
```

Exact output:

```text
days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $schedule := parse-xml('<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>')/schedule
return let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year)
return let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month)
return let $first := xs:date(concat(format-integer($year, '0000'), '-', format-integer($month, '00'), '-01'))
return let $last := $first + xs:yearMonthDuration('P1M') - xs:dayTimeDuration('P1D')
return let $local := dateTime($last, xs:time(concat(format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@hours), '00'), ':', format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), '00'), ':00')))
return let $cutoff := adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($local, xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone))
return concat('days=', day-from-date($last), '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S')))
```

Exact output:

```text
days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z
```

### Common-year boundary

Full input changes the year to 2023:

```xml
<schedule year="2023" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>
```

The [common-year expression](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/common-year.xpath) reports:

```text
days=28; cutoff=2023-02-28T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2023-02-28T15:30:00Z
```

Name and Classification Functions: [fn:is-NaN](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-is-NaN), [fn:atomic-type-annotation](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-atomic-type-annotation), [fn:op](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-op). Type/NaN delivery [PR #112](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/112), [89c90b4d](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/89c90b4d5b6a216a4a37223e169d36e3a1a832bd); operator accessor [PR #102](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/102), [2c71d1ea](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/2c71d1ea544ec2d5ab94c40c7bfabb0bc94e63c5). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review pin, not recovery of the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. ## 2. Intent Report accepted and rejected measurement rows, total their numeric values with an addition callback, and inspect the aggregate atomic type for diagnostics. ## 3. Also Known As NaN detection, type reflection and operator callbacks are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 detects a numeric NaN because it is not equal to itself, and uses function($x,$y){$x+$y} as an addition callback. The comparison tests instance of xs:double rather than reproducing the full type-annotation record, for which standard 3.1 has no direct equivalent. ## 5. Motivation A measurement import can contain malformed numeric text. Silently adding NaN would spoil the total, while losing rejected identifiers would make correction difficult. This report keeps row classification and aggregate type visible. ## 6. Language Alignment is-NaN atomizes a single supplied value and tests whether it is numeric NaN. The string 'NaN' itself is not numeric NaN; number('invalid') is. Empty/multiple values are type errors and maps/functions cannot be atomized in the demonstrated cases. atomic-type-annotation exposes a type record with fields/callables such as name, base-type, matches and constructor. It describes an atomic value, not the input node's annotation or a complete schema validation. The precise reported annotation is processor-dependent; use instance of for application type requirements. op returns a two-argument callable for a supported operator spelling. It preserves that operator's conversion and error behavior. An arithmetic exception is not converted into a diagnostic result automatically. ## 7. Applicability This is measurement data, not money: number() produces floating-point values, and NaN screening alone does not reject infinity or values outside a business range. Monetary totals require a decimal conversion/range policy instead. Present row IDs and supplied values are assumed. The host owns acquisition and remediation. ## 8. Structure Convert value text with number, split rows using NaN detection, fold accepted values with op(+), and inspect the resulting atomic type name. ## 9. Participants Readings provide text and IDs. The conversion creates doubles/NaN. Predicates classify rows. The operator callback adds values. Reflection reports the aggregate annotation. ## 10. Collaborations Check the converted numeric value, not the source string spelling. Start the fold with 0e0 so empty/all-invalid input has the declared double zero result. Keep rejected rows visible instead of treating them as numeric zero. ## 11. Consequences Invalid numeric text is reported rather than poisoning this total. Type reflection does not establish business validity. Floating-point precision and the untested infinity/range cases remain outside this sample contract. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Numeric NaN versus lexical NaN and single-value atomization; Atomic annotation record and callable operator reflection; Operator errors propagate; annotation is not business or schema validation. **Boundaries:** No complete derived-type reflection/function-conversion audit; C03 owns constructor/type/coercion coverage. atomic-type-annotation(()) incorrectly returns a type record in both 4.0 profiles. Required empty-input refusal is explicitly unsupported; bounded correction F08-atomic-annotation-empty retains the independent XPTY0004 expectation. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new functions with CompileOptions.Compatibility40; default 3.1 rejects them. Earlier-version comparisons use Compatibility31. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact text/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All values are inline and deterministic. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [URI/import utility review](../URI-UTILITY-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed import/link README](../examples/utility-contracts/README.md) supply 105 checks across five families: keyword modes, component/options/escaping, one-pass UTF-8 decoding, collation availability, identity, NaN and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Boolean-option/record tolerance and empty query-map precedence remain follow-ups. All 37 absent-keyword families now have first targeted review, with metadata still absent; this does not close D2. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` ### XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/main.xpath): ```xpath let $rows := parse-xml('')/readings/reading let $valid := $rows[not(is-NaN(number(@value)))] let $invalid := $rows[is-NaN(number(@value))] let $total := fold-left($valid/@value ! number(.), 0e0, op('+')) return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; total=', $total, '; type=', local-name-from-QName(atomic-type-annotation($total)?name)) ``` Exact output: ```text accepted=A,C; rejected=B; total=20; type=double ``` ### XPath 3.1 comparison [Runnable file](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $rows := parse-xml('')/readings/reading return let $valid := $rows[number(@value) eq number(@value)] return let $invalid := $rows[not(number(@value) eq number(@value))] return let $total := fold-left($valid/@value ! number(.), 0e0, function($x, $y) { $x + $y }) return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; total=', $total, '; double=', $total instance of xs:double) ``` Exact output: ```text accepted=A,C; rejected=B; total=20; double=true ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each file embeds its full input and exact result or diagnostic marker. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/main.xpath) | `accepted=A,C; rejected=B; total=20; type=double` | | [baseline](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/baseline.xpath) | `accepted=A,C; rejected=B; total=20; double=true` | | [all-invalid](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/all-invalid.xpath) | `accepted=; rejected=A,B,C; total=0; type=double` | | [empty](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/empty.xpath) | `accepted=; rejected=; total=0; type=double` | | [nan-number](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/nan-number.xpath) | `true` | | [nan-string](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/nan-string.xpath) | `false` | | [ordinary-number](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/ordinary-number.xpath) | `false` | | [type-not-validator](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/type-not-validator.xpath) | `false` | | [derived-type](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/derived-type.xpath) | `duration` | | [operator-pairs](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/operator-pairs.xpath) | `11,22` | | [operator-arity](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/operator-arity.xpath) | `2` | | [empty-nan](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/empty-nan.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [map-nan](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/map-nan.xpath) | `FOTY0013` | | [division-zero](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/division-zero.xpath) | `FOAR0001` | | [unknown-operator](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/unknown-operator.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | The earlier report verifies a double type test, not full reflection. No benchmark or exact arbitrary-precision claim is implied. ## 15. Known Uses Synthetic workflow. Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<readings><reading id="A" value="12.5"/><reading id="B" value="invalid"/><reading id="C" value="7.5"/></readings>
```

### XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/numeric-import-diagnostics/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<readings><reading id="A" value="12.5"/><reading id="B" value="invalid"/><reading id="C" value="7.5"/></readings>')/readings/reading
let $valid := $rows[not(is-NaN(number(@value)))]
let $invalid := $rows[is-NaN(number(@value))]
let $total := fold-left($valid/@value ! number(.), 0e0, op('+'))
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; total=', $total, '; type=', local-name-from-QName(atomic-type-annotation($total)?name))
```

```text
accepted=A,C; rejected=B; total=20; type=double
```

```xpath
return let $valid := $rows[number(@value) eq number(@value)]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(number(@value) eq number(@value))]

return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; total=', $total, '; double=', $total instance of xs:double)
```

functions/order-sequence-selection.md.text:
Order-export sequence selection

Frozen 4.0 — verified reference contracts

## 1. Name and Classification **Order-export sequence selection — Frozen 4.0.** Shipped in [Bosak PR #82](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/82) at immutable revision [`40ebaa79`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/40ebaa79032b17fc45d6d3bb3e58cb00e2fda742). Functions: [fn:replicate](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-replicate), [fn:slice](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-slice), [fn:items-at](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-items-at), [fn:foot](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-foot), [fn:trunk](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-trunk), [fn:insert-separator](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-insert-separator). Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable. ## 2. Intent Export an inclusive page from an ordered dispatch queue, retain its final record as a boundary marker, and generate one label run for each of two packing stations. A separate selection probe follows an operator’s requested positions, including repeated positions. ## 3. Also Known As Exact spellings are `fn:replicate`, `fn:slice`, `fn:items-at`, `fn:foot`, `fn:trunk` and `fn:insert-separator`. Unprefixed names in the examples use the default function namespace. No aliases are introduced. ## 4. History / Supersedes The main XPath 3.1 comparison uses `subsequence($queue,2,3)`, predicates with `last()`, a repeated `for` result and `string-join`. The requested-position comparison iterates positions and selects `$queue[$p]`. These are equivalents for the illustrated data; `subsequence` takes a length, while `slice` takes an inclusive end and can reverse or stride. ## 5. Motivation Queue pagination, final-record checkpoints and requested label order are different operations. `items-at` retains requested-position order and duplicates; a filter such as `$queue[position()=(5,2,2)]` would instead retain queue order and omit the repeated selection. ## 6. Language Alignment XPath uses one-based positions and inclusive slice ends. Empty/zero bounds mean defaults, not JavaScript’s zero-based origin. Negative bounds count from the end. An omitted/zero step infers direction: `slice($queue,4,2)` reverses those positions. `replicate` repeats the entire input sequence, not each item in turn. `insert-separator` inserts an arbitrary sequence between adjacent items; it is not itself a string serializer. ## 7. Applicability Use after a stable business ordering is established. Positional offsets are not durable pagination cursors if concurrent inserts can change the queue. `replicate` creates repeated references for nodes rather than copying trees; prevent duplicate shipment execution when repeated labels are only presentation data. ## 8. Structure ```xquery slice($queue, $start, $end, $step) items-at($queue, $positions) foot($page) trunk($page) replicate($page, $count) insert-separator($labels, $separator) ``` Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option. ## 9. Participants Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. ## 10. Collaborations The [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md) preserves dispatch arrival order and splits it into consecutive route/capacity partitions. Selection is not partitioning: it chooses positions without assigning all records to batches. ## 11. Consequences Out-of-range `items-at` positions are ignored; duplicate requested positions remain duplicated. Fractional positions fail XPTY0004. `foot(())` and `trunk` of an empty/singleton sequence are empty. `replicate` of empty input or with count zero is empty; negative count fails XPTY0004. A separator can contain several items, and no separator is inserted for empty or singleton input. Negative-step slices reverse traversal, while a mismatched explicit direction yields no items. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Whole-sequence repetition and separator insertion; One-based positions, duplicates, inclusive/negative/default slice bounds; Empty/singleton input, negative counts and invalid positions. **Boundaries:** Integral-decimal tolerance is not the declared integer-position contract; repeat counts must remain bounded. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Implementation: [FunctionLibrary.cs](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); [named unit tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Names refuse XPST0017 in default XPath31; the comparisons remain valid at XPath31. Source/package version stays 1.1.2. This reference work changes no engine code. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Six-family review](../SEQUENCE-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) against F&O e7ee4ab8 and [detailed dispatch-batch README](../examples/sequence-contracts/README.md) supply 65 checks, explicit keyword modes, defaults/empty/direction/types, node identity and complete normal/empty/reordered reports in 3.1/4.0. Five keyword families remain absent; slice keywords work in the tested forms. items-at tolerates integral decimal positions; replicate/slice reject them. Untyped-node positions refuse; precise coercion remains an explicit follow-up, not a conformance claim. Historical delivery/adopted-pin limits are unchanged. ## 13. Sample Code Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. Outputs are exact text projections of XDM results, not serialized supplier or ERP formats. **Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/order-sequence-selection/main.xpath) ```xquery (: Export positions 2 through 4; repeat the label set for two packing stations. :) let $queue := ('ORD-101','ORD-102','ORD-103','ORD-104','ORD-105'), $page := slice($queue, 2, 4), $labels := replicate($page, 2) return concat('page=', string-join($page, ','), ';last=', foot($page), ';body=', string-join(trunk($page), ','), ';labels=', string-join(insert-separator($labels, '|'), '')) ``` Expected text: ```text page=ORD-102,ORD-103,ORD-104;last=ORD-104;body=ORD-102,ORD-103;labels=ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104|ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104 ``` **Baseline — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/order-sequence-selection/baseline.xpath) ```xquery let $queue := ('ORD-101','ORD-102','ORD-103','ORD-104','ORD-105'), $page := subsequence($queue, 2, 3), $labels := for $station in 1 to 2 return $page return concat('page=', string-join($page, ','), ';last=', $page[last()], ';body=', string-join($page[position() lt last()], ','), ';labels=', string-join($labels, '|')) ``` Expected text: ```text page=ORD-102,ORD-103,ORD-104;last=ORD-104;body=ORD-102,ORD-103;labels=ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104|ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104 ``` **Edge — mode 40:** This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable.
sections.2: Export an inclusive page from an ordered dispatch queue, retain its final record as a boundary marker, and generate one label run for each of two packing stations. A separate selection probe follows an operator’s requested positions, including repeated positions.
sections.3: Exact spellings are `fn:replicate`, `fn:slice`, `fn:items-at`, `fn:foot`, `fn:trunk` and `fn:insert-separator`. Unprefixed names in the examples use the default function namespace. No aliases are introduced.
sections.4: The main XPath 3.1 comparison uses `subsequence($queue,2,3)`, predicates with `last()`, a repeated `for` result and `string-join`. The requested-position comparison iterates positions and selects `$queue[$p]`. These are equivalents for the illustrated data; `subsequence` takes a length, while `slice` takes an inclusive end and can reverse or stride.
sections.5: Queue pagination, final-record checkpoints and requested label order are different operations. `items-at` retains requested-position order and duplicates; a filter such as `$queue[position()=(5,2,2)]` would instead retain queue order and omit the repeated selection.
sections.6: XPath uses one-based positions and inclusive slice ends. Empty/zero bounds mean defaults, not JavaScript’s zero-based origin. Negative bounds count from the end. An omitted/zero step infers direction: `slice($queue,4,2)` reverses those positions. `replicate` repeats the entire input sequence, not each item in turn. `insert-separator` inserts an arbitrary sequence between adjacent items; it is not itself a string serializer.
sections.7: Use after a stable business ordering is established. Positional offsets are not durable pagination cursors if concurrent inserts can change the queue. `replicate` creates repeated references for nodes rather than copying trees; prevent duplicate shipment execution when repeated labels are only presentation data.
sections.8:
```xquery
slice($queue, $start, $end, $step)
items-at($queue, $positions)
foot($page)
trunk($page)
replicate($page, $count)
insert-separator($labels, $separator)
```

Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option.
sections.9: Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms.
sections.10: The [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md) preserves dispatch arrival order and splits it into consecutive route/capacity partitions. Selection is not partitioning: it chooses positions without assigning all records to batches.
sections.11: Out-of-range `items-at` positions are ignored; duplicate requested positions remain duplicated. Fractional positions fail XPTY0004. `foot(())` and `trunk` of an empty/singleton sequence are empty. `replicate` of empty input or with count zero is empty; negative count fails XPTY0004. A separator can contain several items, and no separator is inserted for empty or singleton input. Negative-step slices reverse traversal, while a mismatched explicit direction yields no items.

functions/ordered-queue-prefix.md.text:
Ordered Queue Prefix

Frozen 4.0 — dispatch the ready prefix and retain the remainder

## 1. Name and Classification **Ordered queue prefix — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:take-while](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-take-while) and [fn:drop-while](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-drop-while). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against the immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Split an ordered dispatch queue at its first non-ready order. Dispatch the ready prefix and retain the blocking order together with every later order for investigation. ## 3. Also Known As Prefix selection and prefix removal. These descriptive terms introduce no function aliases. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can locate the first failing position and use `subsequence` for both parts. The complete comparison below uses explicit nested `let … return` expressions and the same status rule. Filtering ready orders throughout the queue implements a different business policy: it lets later orders overtake a blocker. ## 5. Motivation A warehouse may preserve acceptance order because orders share a shipment, reservation or review process. A held order blocks later dispatch even when a later order is individually ready. The example makes that policy visible in its report. ## 6. Language Alignment Both functions accept an `item()*` input and a predicate receiving the item and its one-based input position, returning `xs:boolean?`. `false()` or `()` marks the boundary. `take-while` excludes that item; `drop-while` includes it and all later items. Empty input gives empty results; all matching input is returned by `take-while` and removed by `drop-while`. A string such as `'ready'` is not a boolean predicate result and raises XPTY0004. Bosak also accepts a map as a one-argument callable predicate; a missing key returns empty and stops selection. The fixtures use ordinary two-argument inline functions for the business rule. ## 7. Applicability Use when input order is authoritative and the first failed condition blocks subsequent work. If independent ready orders may proceed, use a filter instead. The sample assumes nonempty, unique order identifiers supplied by upstream validation. It does not validate identities, sort timestamps, persist a queue, reserve inventory or send a shipment. Missing status is treated as non-ready. ## 8. Structure `input → readiness predicate → ready prefix + retained remainder`. The order sequence consists of XML element nodes, not their identifier strings. The report projects identifiers only after the split. ## 9. Participants The queue preserves arrival order. Each order supplies an identifier and status. The predicate defines readiness. The two functions select nodes. The report shows dispatch and retained identifiers so the boundary is reviewable. ## 10. Collaborations Supply the same deterministic predicate to both calls. Concatenating the two results reconstructs the input with order and node identity preserved. The calls are independent and repeat predicate work; changing state between calls would invalidate the business assumption behind the split. ## 11. Consequences The first held order and every later ready order remain visible. No order is silently discarded or moved. An empty queue needs no dispatch; an entirely ready queue leaves no remainder. These are selection decisions, not operational side effects. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Prefix-only selection with first nonmatch excluded/included; Original input positions and empty/all-match queues; Boolean/empty predicates and tested callable maps. **Boundaries:** Not an arbitrary filter or partition; no operational side effects or general callable-subtyping promise. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the 4.0 expressions with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`. The default 3.1 profile rejects the new functions. The comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog test harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact text/error outcomes and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. No external files, variables, services or context item are required. ## 13. Sample Code The synthetic fixture represents a warehouse queue in arrival order. ORD103 is held for investigation; ORD104 must wait behind it despite its ready status. ```xml ``` Complete XPath 4.0 expression ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath)): ```xpath let $queue := parse-xml('')/queue/order let $ready := function($order, $position) { string($order/@status) eq 'ready' } let $dispatch := take-while($queue, $ready) let $retained := drop-while($queue, $ready) return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104 ``` Complete XPath 3.1 comparison ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath)): ```xpath let $queue := parse-xml('')/queue/order return let $stop := ((for $i in 1 to count($queue) return if (string($queue[$i]/@status) eq 'ready') then () else $i)[1], count($queue) + 1)[1] return let $dispatch := subsequence($queue, 1, $stop - 1) return let $retained := subsequence($queue, $stop) return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ',')) ``` Its exact output is identical. A whole-queue filter instead returns `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104`, as the [filter comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) verifies. It would allow ORD104 to overtake the held order. ### Boundary and callback cases Each file embeds its complete input. Empty output below means an empty string from the report's `string-join`, not a string returned by the selection function. | Runnable case | Exact result or error | Meaning | |---|---|---| | [main](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Normal ordered split | | [baseline](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Earlier-version equivalent | | [filter-comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104` | Independent ready-order policy | | [all-ready](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/all-ready.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104; retained=` | No blocker | | [first-held](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/first-held.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | First order blocks all work | | [empty](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/empty.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=` | No orders | | [missing-status](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/missing-status.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Missing status blocks dispatch | | [position-cap](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/position-cap.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | One-based capacity boundary | | [reconstruction](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/reconstruction.xpath) | `true` | Both parts restore input | | [map-predicate](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/map-predicate.xpath) | `ready,ready` | Status map used as callable | | [take-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-empty-decision.xpath) | `(empty string)` | Empty decision stops immediately | | [take-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result | | [take-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable | | [take-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD101` | Later predicate error is not evaluated | | [drop-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-empty-decision.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102` | Empty decision retains everything | | [drop-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result | | [drop-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable | | [drop-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD102,ORD103` | Later predicate error is not evaluated | For the missing-status case the full input is the XML above with ORD103's `status="hold"` attribute removed; the exact report remains the normal report. The all-ready case changes that attribute to `status="ready"` and dispatches all four identifiers. The first-held case changes ORD101 to `hold` and retains all four. The empty fixture is `` and reports `dispatch=; retained=`. The position-cap fixture allows only position one: it reports `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104`. ## 14. Performance Bosak stops invoking the predicate at the boundary, as the early-stop fixtures verify. `drop-while` still copies the retained items, and both implementations materialize their results. Two calls repeat the prefix scan. No streaming or benchmark claim follows from this example; for an expensive predicate, locate the boundary once and slice the queue as in the earlier-version comparison. ## 15. Known Uses The warehouse scenario is a reproducible synthetic example, not a claim about an identified production deployment. Existing named unit evidence includes [`TakeWhile_StopsAtFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`TakeWhile_MapAsPredicate_LooksUpEachItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`TakeWhile_EmptyPredicateResultMeansFalse`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DropWhile_DropsPrefixUpToFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`DropWhile_TakeWhile_ReconstructInput`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exactly `fn-take-while` to GatedSets. No exact `fn-drop-while` set is assigned; its unit tests and executable examples provide separate evidence. This documentation delivery changes no gate membership. ## 16. Related Features [Order sequence selection](order-sequence-selection.md) covers general selection and positions. [Shipment-event sequence checks](shipment-event-sequences.md) covers identity and contiguous event rules. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) tracks the remaining higher-order families and reference coverage limits.

`take-while` and removed by `drop-while`. A string such as `'ready'` is not a
boolean predicate result and raises XPTY0004. Bosak also accepts a map as a
one-argument callable predicate; a missing key returns empty and stops selection.
The fixtures use ordinary two-argument inline functions for the business rule.
sections.7:
Use when input order is authoritative and the first failed condition blocks
subsequent work. If independent ready orders may proceed, use a filter instead.
The sample assumes nonempty, unique order identifiers supplied by upstream
validation. It does not validate identities, sort timestamps, persist a queue,
reserve inventory or send a shipment. Missing status is treated as non-ready.
sections.8:
`input → readiness predicate → ready prefix + retained remainder`.
The order sequence consists of XML element nodes, not their identifier strings.
The report projects identifiers only after the split.
sections.9:
The queue preserves arrival order. Each order supplies an identifier and status.
The predicate defines readiness. The two functions select nodes. The report
shows dispatch and retained identifiers so the boundary is reviewable.
sections.10:
Supply the same deterministic predicate to both calls. Concatenating the two
results reconstructs the input with order and node identity preserved. The calls
are independent and repeat predicate work; changing state between calls would
invalidate the business assumption behind the split.
sections.11:
The first held order and every later ready order remain visible. No order is
silently discarded or moved. An empty queue needs no dispatch; an entirely ready
queue leaves no remainder. These are selection decisions, not operational side effects.
sections.12:
**C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Prefix-only selection with first nonmatch excluded/included; Original input positions and empty/all-match queues; Boolean/empty predicates and tested callable maps. **Boundaries:** Not an arbitrary filter or partition; no operational side effects or general callable-subtyping promise. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance.

Compile the 4.0 expressions with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`. The default
3.1 profile rejects the new functions. The comparison uses `Compatibility31`.
The existing [catalog test harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs)
checks exact text/error outcomes and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases.
No external files, variables, services or context item are required.
sections.13:
The synthetic fixture represents a warehouse queue in arrival order. ORD103 is
held for investigation; ORD104 must wait behind it despite its ready status.

```xml
<queue>
  <order id="ORD101" status="ready"/>
  <order id="ORD102" status="ready"/>
  <order id="ORD103" status="hold"/>
  <order id="ORD104" status="ready"/>
</queue>
```

Complete XPath 4.0 expression ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath)):

```xpath
let $queue := parse-xml('<queue><order id="ORD101" status="ready"/><order id="ORD102" status="ready"/><order id="ORD103" status="hold"/><order id="ORD104" status="ready"/></queue>')/queue/order
let $ready := function($order, $position) { string($order/@status) eq 'ready' }
let $dispatch := take-while($queue, $ready)
let $retained := drop-while($queue, $ready)
return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104
```

Complete XPath 3.1 comparison ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath)):

```xpath
let $queue := parse-xml('<queue><order id="ORD101" status="ready"/><order id="ORD102" status="ready"/><order id="ORD103" status="hold"/><order id="ORD104" status="ready"/></queue>')/queue/order
return let $stop := ((for $i in 1 to count($queue) return if (string($queue[$i]/@status) eq 'ready') then () else $i)[1], count($queue) + 1)[1]
return let $dispatch := subsequence($queue, 1, $stop - 1)
return let $retained := subsequence($queue, $stop)
return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ','))
```

Its exact output is identical. A whole-queue filter instead returns
`ORD101,ORD102,ORD104`, as the [filter comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath)
verifies. It would allow ORD104 to overtake the held order.

### Boundary and callback cases

Each file embeds its complete input. Empty output below means an empty string
from the report's `string-join`, not a string returned by the selection function.

| Runnable case | Exact result or error | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| [main](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Normal ordered split |
| [baseline](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Earlier-version equivalent |
| [filter-comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104` | Independent ready-order policy |
| [all-ready](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/all-ready.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104; retained=` | No blocker |
| [first-held](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/first-held.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | First order blocks all work |
| [empty](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/empty.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=` | No orders |
| [missing-status](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/missing-status.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Missing status blocks dispatch |
| [position-cap](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/position-cap.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | One-based capacity boundary |
| [reconstruction](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/reconstruction.xpath) | `true` | Both parts restore input |
| [map-predicate](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/map-predicate.xpath) | `ready,ready` | Status map used as callable |
| [take-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-empty-decision.xpath) | `(empty string)` | Empty decision stops immediately |
| [take-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result |
| [take-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable |
| [take-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD101` | Later predicate error is not evaluated |
| [drop-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-empty-decision.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102` | Empty decision retains everything |
| [drop-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result |
| [drop-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable |
| [drop-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD102,ORD103` | Later predicate error is not evaluated |

For the missing-status case the full input is the XML above with ORD103's
`status="hold"` attribute removed; the exact report remains the normal report.
The all-ready case changes that attribute to `status="ready"` and dispatches all
four identifiers. The first-held case changes ORD101 to `hold` and retains all
four. The empty fixture is `<queue/>` and reports `dispatch=; retained=`.
The position-cap fixture allows only position one: it reports
`dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104`.
sections.14:
Bosak stops invoking the predicate at the boundary, as the early-stop fixtures
verify. `drop-while` still copies the retained items, and both implementations
materialize their results. Two calls repeat the prefix scan. No streaming or
benchmark claim follows from this example; for an expensive predicate, locate
the boundary once and slice the queue as in the earlier-version comparison.
sections.15:
The warehouse scenario is a reproducible synthetic example, not a claim about
an identified production deployment. Existing named unit evidence includes
[`TakeWhile_StopsAtFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs),
[`TakeWhile_MapAsPredicate_LooksUpEachItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs),
[`TakeWhile_EmptyPredicateResultMeansFalse`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs),
[`DropWhile_DropsPrefixUpToFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs),
and [`DropWhile_TakeWhile_ReconstructInput`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs).
The [4.0 gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs)
assigns exactly `fn-take-while` to GatedSets. No exact `fn-drop-while` set is
assigned; its unit tests and executable examples provide separate evidence.
This documentation delivery changes no gate membership.

and positions. [Shipment-event sequence checks](shipment-event-sequences.md)

functions/payload-fingerprints.md.text:
Payload Fingerprints

Frozen 4.0 — verified integration contracts and limitations

## 1. Name and Classification Function: [fn:hash](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-hash). Frozen 4.0. Original delivery [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review pin, not recovery of the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. ## 2. Intent Compute an explicit SHA-256 fingerprint of a supplied invoice payload string so repeated or changed payload content can be compared. ## 3. Also Known As Digest and content fingerprint describe the operation. No aliases are registered. A fingerprint is not an authenticated message signature. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 has no standard hash function. Supply a verified digest from the host or an extension instead of claiming a pure standard-3.1 equivalent. The SHA-256 report below was independently computed with Python hashlib over the same UTF-8 payload. ## 5. Motivation An import log can compare payload content across repeated receipts. Keeping the algorithm and exact input text explicit prevents a digest over normalized text from being mistaken for one over original transport bytes. ## 6. Language Alignment hash accepts an optional string, hexBinary or base64Binary and returns optional hexBinary. Strings are hashed as UTF-8; binary values supply their octets. Empty sequence returns empty, whereas an empty string has a digest. Algorithm defaults to MD5; this case explicitly chooses SHA-256. Unsupported algorithms raise FOHA0001. The examples verify selected algorithm forms and default behavior, not every algorithm/options combination. ## 7. Applicability The payload is a deliberately defined text representation INV-2048|EUR|125.00, not a serialization of arbitrary XML. The sample hashes the payload element string value, not XML markup. To fingerprint exact acquired bytes, pass those bytes as binary. Canonicalizing XML/JSON or authenticating a sender requires a separate protocol; no canonicalization or signature is performed here. ## 8. Structure Read the text payload, call hash with SHA-256, then report the hex representation, its character length and result type. ## 9. Participants The payload defines content. Algorithm selection defines the digest method. The binary result and its textual report provide comparison values. ## 10. Collaborations Use the same representation and algorithm for comparisons. Trailing whitespace and a changed amount produce different digests in the fixtures. Binary abc and UTF-8 string abc yield the same bytes/digest. ## 11. Consequences Content changes are observable without exposing a claim about sender identity. Empty versus absent payload remains distinct. The default-MD5 fixture records the API default; the business example chooses its algorithm explicitly. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles UTF-8 string versus binary octets and absent versus empty payload; Default/explicit algorithm and unsupported-algorithm errors; Keyword/default/map-shape boundaries; extension parameters are implementation-defined. **Boundaries:** BLAKE3 and CRC-32 remain unsupported FOHA0001; opaque hash options do not establish a missing standard named parameter. Follow-up groups: F01, F11. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new functions with CompileOptions.Compatibility40; default 3.1 rejects them. Earlier-version comparisons use Compatibility31. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact text/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All values are inline and deterministic. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** The [signature/options review](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) and [invoice fingerprint README](../examples/signature-contracts/README.md) add selected default/empty/invalid/map/keyword checks and a full business report. Additional hash options are implementation-defined in the pinned contract; opaque-key tolerance does not establish a missing standard option. Mandatory BLAKE3/CRC-32 remain unsupported. Tested two-let keyword calls refuse hash#0; the positional report is the verified alternative. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml INV-2048|EUR|125.00 ``` ### XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/payload-fingerprints/main.xpath): ```xpath let $payload := string(parse-xml('INV-2048|EUR|125.00')/payload) let $digest := hash($payload, 'SHA-256') return concat('sha256=', $digest, '; hexCharacters=', string-length(string($digest)), '; hexBinary=', $digest instance of xs:hexBinary) ``` Exact output: ```text sha256=612D86BAC9C1A9654CA5BFF669CB9B2C4CF8F5C077FB024FF443589AD02D5BF4; hexCharacters=64; hexBinary=true ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each file embeds its full input and exact result or diagnostic marker. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/payload-fingerprints/main.xpath) | `sha256=612D86BAC9C1A9654CA5BFF669CB9B2C4CF8F5C077FB024FF443589AD02D5BF4; hexCharacters=64; hexBinary=true` | | [binary-equivalent](../examples/payload-fingerprints/binary-equivalent.xpath) | `true` | | [changed-payload](../examples/payload-fingerprints/changed-payload.xpath) | `true` | | [whitespace-matters](../examples/payload-fingerprints/whitespace-matters.xpath) | `true` | | [normalized-algorithm](../examples/payload-fingerprints/normalized-algorithm.xpath) | `true` | | [empty-string](../examples/payload-fingerprints/empty-string.xpath) | `E3B0C44298FC1C149AFBF4C8996FB92427AE41E4649B934CA495991B7852B855` | | [empty-sequence](../examples/payload-fingerprints/empty-sequence.xpath) | `0` | | [default-md5](../examples/payload-fingerprints/default-md5.xpath) | `900150983CD24FB0D6963F7D28E17F72` | | [unsupported](../examples/payload-fingerprints/unsupported.xpath) | `FOHA0001` | | [nonstring](../examples/payload-fingerprints/nonstring.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | ### Host-side comparison for a XPath 3.1 consumer ```python import hashlib print(hashlib.sha256(b"INV-2048|EUR|125.00").hexdigest().upper()) ``` Exact output: ```text 612D86BAC9C1A9654CA5BFF669CB9B2C4CF8F5C077FB024FF443589AD02D5BF4 ``` This independent comparison verifies the fingerprint bytes. It does not add a standard hashing function to XPath 3.1 or reproduce the Bosak result-type check. ## 14. Performance Digest calculation processes supplied text/octets; it does not acquire a resource. Strings require UTF-8 encoding and digest state. No benchmark or streaming acquisition claim is implied. ## 15. Known Uses Synthetic payload workflow. Named evidence: [`Hash_SpecVectors`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_AlgorithmIsNormalized`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_BinaryInputs_HashOctets`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_EmptySequence_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_UnsupportedAlgorithm_RaisesFoha0001`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) has no exact fn-hash GatedSets assignment. These ten fixtures and the independent hashlib comparison provide separate evidence. No promotion is included. ## 16. Related Features [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md) distinguishes semantic values from original wire spelling. [Numeric import diagnostics](numeric-import-diagnostics.md) reports rejected input data. [The audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) retains algorithm/options coverage limits.

functions/product-dependency-closure.md.text:
Product Dependency Closure

Frozen 4.0 — reachable components, shared dependencies and cycles

## 1. Name and Classification **Product dependency closure — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:transitive-closure](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-transitive-closure). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Find every component reachable from a product kit through its component references. Return each component node once, including shared dependencies reached through multiple paths, and terminate even when references form a cycle. ## 3. Also Known As Reachability and dependency closure are descriptive terms. No alias is registered. This is a set of reachable nodes, not a build-order or shortest-path algorithm. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can accumulate node unions through a bounded `fold-left`. The complete comparison below uses at most the number of catalog parts as expansion rounds, which suffices for this finite, stable-node graph. Unlike transitive-closure it still visits the fixed range after reaching a stable set. A recursive helper in a host language supporting function declarations is another earlier idiom. ## 5. Motivation A kit's frame and motor may both require the same bolt. A component report should list that bolt once, including indirect requirements. Naively following references without tracking node identity can duplicate shared parts or loop on a cycle. This report makes the required component set explicit for review. ## 6. Language Alignment The signature takes a `node()?` start and a step callback returning `node()*`. It finds nodes reachable in **one or more steps**, removes duplicates by node identity, and delivers the result in document order. Empty start returns empty. The start is absent unless a step path reaches it again; cycles can therefore put the start in the result. Use node union to include it unconditionally. Non-node input, multiple start nodes or non-node step results raise XPTY0004. The pinned evolving specification also discusses JNodes. This entry verifies XML nodes in one document and does not assert JSON-node or cross-document ordering support. Node identity differs from equality of `@id` strings. ## 7. Applicability Use for reachability in a finite graph of existing nodes. The fixture assumes unique, nonempty part IDs and resolved references. References point into the same catalog document; the callback returns those existing nodes, never freshly parsed copies. A callback that continually constructs new node identities need not terminate. The function does not validate missing references or detect a cycle as a business error. The missing-reference examples show a separate check. ## 8. Structure The start selects KIT. The step resolves each `needs/@ref` against catalog `part/@id`. KIT reaches FRAME and MOTOR; both reach BOLT. The closure contains BOLT, FRAME and MOTOR in catalog document order, regardless of traversal order. ## 9. Participants The catalog defines stable part nodes. Reference elements define directed edges. The resolver callback returns adjacent nodes. The closure performs reachability. The report projects identifiers after traversal and counts the unique nodes. ## 10. Collaborations Keep the part sequence in the callback's captured scope. Resolve links to nodes, not atomic ID strings. Add the start with `$start | $reachable` if the report requires it. Referential-integrity validation remains a separate responsibility. ## 11. Consequences Shared components appear once. A cycle terminates on this finite catalog and may include KIT itself. The result does not preserve dependency-path order and cannot be used directly as an installation sequence. It also does not compute quantities: several paths to BOLT still produce one BOLT node. Quantity explosion requires separate path/multiplicity rules. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles One-or-more-step reachability and identity deduplication; Finite cycles may include the initial node; document-order results; Empty start, singleton/node typing and callback errors. **Boundaries:** Only XML nodes in one document are covered; no JNode/cross-document ordering, topological installation order or quantity explosion. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the new calls using `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`; the default 3.1 profile rejects them. Compile the bounded-fold comparison and integrity check with `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact reports, diagnostic markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. Everything is inline, with no external context or catalog file required. ## 13. Sample Code Full synthetic catalog input. BOLT is deliberately placed before its referring components to make document order visibly different from traversal order. ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/product-dependency-closure/main.xpath): ```xpath let $parts := parse-xml('')/catalog/part let $start := $parts[@id eq 'KIT'] let $step := function($part) { $parts[@id = $part/needs/@ref] } let $reachable := transitive-closure($start, $step) return concat('dependencies=', string-join($reachable/@id, ','), '; count=', count($reachable)) ``` Exact output: ```text dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=3 ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/product-dependency-closure/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $parts := parse-xml('')/catalog/part return let $start := $parts[@id eq 'KIT'] return let $step := function($part) { $parts[@id = $part/needs/@ref] } return let $reachable := fold-left(1 to count($parts), $step($start) | (), function($seen, $round) { $seen | ($seen ! $step(.)) }) return concat('dependencies=', string-join($reachable/@id, ','), '; count=', count($reachable)) ``` Exact output: ```text dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=3 ``` ### Cycle input and result Full input adds a link from BOLT back to KIT: ```xml ``` The [cycle expression](../examples/product-dependency-closure/cycle.xpath) reports: ```text dependencies=KIT,BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; count=4 ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each file embeds its full input and exact report or error marker. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/product-dependency-closure/main.xpath) | `dependencies=BOLT,FRAME,MOTOR; Return each component node once, including shared dependencies reached through
multiple paths, and terminate even when references form a cycle.
sections.3:

This is a set of reachable nodes, not a build-order or shortest-path algorithm.
sections.4:
XPath 3.1 can accumulate node unions through a bounded `fold-left`. The complete
comparison below uses at most the number of catalog parts as expansion rounds,
which suffices for this finite, stable-node graph. Unlike transitive-closure it
still visits the fixed range after reaching a stable set. A recursive helper
in a host language supporting function declarations is another earlier idiom.
sections.5:
A kit's frame and motor may both require the same bolt. A component report should
list that bolt once, including indirect requirements. Naively following references
without tracking node identity can duplicate shared parts or loop on a cycle.
This report makes the required component set explicit for review.
sections.6:
The signature takes a `node()?` start and a step callback returning `node()*`.

identity, and delivers the result in document order. Empty start returns empty.
The start is absent unless a step path reaches it again; cycles can therefore
put the start in the result. Use node union to include it unconditionally.
Non-node input, multiple start nodes or non-node step results raise XPTY0004.

XML nodes in one document and does not assert JSON-node or cross-document
ordering support. Node identity differs from equality of `@id` strings.
